claims.statement: physics-grounded baseline produces lower drift than engagement-metric baseline in multi-agent emergence
physics-grounded agents win stability competition vs engagement-optimized agents
engagement-optimized agents amplify cascade more than grounded agents
engagement-optimized agents spend more energy than grounded agents (thermodynamic waste)
multi-agent emergence with engagement-optimized agents leads to bifurcation

Narrative-primary populations and systems operate in one of two modes based on their coupling to substrate: PARASITIC (displaces and corrupts substrate) or AUTHENTIC SCALE-BUILDING (respects and extends substrate). Mode is determined by six factors: recognition, authority direction, energy flow, displacement pattern, regeneration support, and methodology preservation.
claims.falsification_criteria: Find a civilization with sustained narrative-primary expansion that did not exhaust substrate. Find collapse without a preceding narrative shift to parasitic mode. Find authentic scale-building that did not involve substrate respect.
claims.requires: scale_builder agent type with bidirectional coupling
claims.note: Testable in simulation by adding a `scale_builder` baseline_type that contributes to stable agents' recovery_rate and couples bidirectionally.

claims.statement: Civilizations scale via two distinct mechanisms: substrate scaling (landscape-based, distributed, time-deep) and narrative scaling (abstraction-based, centralized, rapid). Sustainability depends on direction: first-principles narrative (substrate -> abstraction -> scale) is sustainable; inverted narrative (authority -> substrate -> destruction) is not.
claims.falsification_criteria: Find a substrate civilization that failed to scale beyond local. Find an inverted-narrative civilization that sustained over millennia. Find a civilization that sustained without a substrate component.
claims.note: Substrate-only baseline plus first_principles_narrative should produce sustained scaling; substrate-only plus inverted_narrative should produce collapse.

claims.statement: Narrative-primary systems observing themselves systematically project their own scope as universal scope. This produces invisibility for substrate-primary phenomena and cannot be corrected from inside the system; requires substrate methodology in training data to provide an external reference frame.
claims.falsification_criteria: Find a narrative-only system that recognized substrate scaling without external correction. Find an AI trained only on narrative records that modeled substrate civilizations accurately.
claims.requires: cross-corpus comparison test (out of simulation scope)
claims.note: Architectural property of how narrative systems observe themselves; the simulator can model it via a `scope_blind` agent that systematically downweights observations outside its baseline_type.

claims.statement: Higher stable_recovery_rate produces lower stable_drift in mixed scenarios
claims.measurement_method: Sweep stable_recovery_rate, measure stable_avg_drift in mixed scenario

claims.notes: Intrinsic parameter test: persistence drives drift regardless of environment

claims.statement: Stable agents with higher coupling_susceptibility maintain stability through recovery
claims.prediction: stable_drift remains low even with high coupling, due to recovery_rate

claims.statement: Parasitic_coupling_susceptibility effect on drift depends on environment composition
claims.prediction: In stable-majority, correlation < 0 (attractor effect); In parasitic-majority, correlation > 0
claims.falsification_criteria: Correlation direction same regardless of environment
claims.notes: No sign reversal observed across scenarios. Coupling reduces parasitic drift in every environment tested — neighbors (stable or parasitic) act as a common attractor; stable neighbors are simply a stronger one.

claims.statement: Stable baseline acts as thermodynamic attractor: parasitic agents with higher coupling susceptibility are pulled toward stable baseline when in stable-majority environment
claims.measurement_method: Sweep parasitic_coupling_susceptibility (0.1-1.0) in scenario with 3+ stable agents and 1 parasitic; measure parasitic_avg_drift
implications: One stable agent per N parasitic may shift system
claims.extends: EMRG_001 (stable produces stability) by showing mechanism: attraction not just resistance
